caseno: Civil Petition For Leave To Appeal No. 360 of 1994
lawyer:
Mr. Khondker Mahbubuddin Ahmed, Senior Advocate, instructed by Mr. Shamsul Haque Siddique, Advocate-on-Record ----- For the Petitioner.
Respondents: Not represented.
parties:
Sheikh Abu Sayyid ----- Defendant No. 2— Petitioner
Vs.
Sonali Bank and others ----- Plaintiff-Respondents
full_judgment:
Latifur Rahman, J: Defendant No.2 petitioner calls in question the judgment dated 24.4.1994 passed by a Single Judge of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 8122 of 1991 affirming the order dated 15.8.91 passed by the Second Artha Rin Adalat, Khulna in Title Suit No. 5 of 1990 modifying the final mortgage decree dated 15.6.91 passed in the suit upon an application of defendant No.3 under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure. 

 2. Respondent No. 1, Sonali Bank instituted Title Suit No. 189 of 1980 in the Court of Subordinate Judge, Khulna against the petitioner firm and respondent No. 3 for recovery of Tk. 2,14,966.70 advanced against mortgage of immovable property belonging to defendant respondent No. 3 The suit was ultimately transferred to the 2nd Artha Rin Adalat, Khulna and re-numbered as Title Suit No. 5 of 1990 of that Court. The suit was decreed in preliminary form by judgment dated 13.9.90 for an amount of Tk. 2,14,966.70 with interest. 

 3. Defendant-respondent No. 3 filed an application on 12.5.91 for sale of the attached properties of the petitioner first (which had been attached before judgment), but no order was passed thereon and the preliminary decree was made final on 15.6.91 directing recovery of the decretal dues by sale of the mortgaged property belonging to the defendant respondent No. 3 as described in schedule "A" to the plaint. 

 4. There was no appeal against the afore-said final decree dated 15.6.91. Defendant No. 3 filed an application before the trial court under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure on 7.8.91 for review of the order dated 15.6.91 praying for setting aside the order and to realise the decretal amount by sale of like property of the petitioner attached before judgment as per observation made by the High Court Division in the aforesaid Civil Revision No. 221 of 1984. After hearing the parties, the learned trial court allowed the application filed by respondent No. 3 and directed sale of the property of the petitioner (attached before judgment) first and for sale of the mortgaged property only after failure to recover the whole decretal amount from such safe of the petitioners property. This order as actinide in revision. 

 5. Mr. Khondker Mahbubuddin Ahmed, learned Advocate submits that in view of the provisions of Rule (4), (5) and (6) of Order XXXIV of the Code of Civil Procedure, the final decree passed in the suit for sale having been made absolute the trial court became functus officio, except in the cases of fraud and mistake of court, and there being no such fraud or mistake the trial court erred in law in re-viewing the final decree upon an application under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure and the High Court Division erred in affirming such erroneous order of the trial court. 

 6. It appears that defendant No. 2 petitioner is the real borrower of plaintiff-bank. Defendant No. 3 was the guarantor of the loanee being the said Firm. It has already been mentioned that in F.M.A. No. 1 of 1986 order of attachment of the personal property of defendant No, 2 was maintained as the real relief of the Plaintiff-bank lies against the property of defendant No. 2 as a debtor. The learned Single Judge of the High Court Division correctly held that the court is bound to sell the mortgaged property first and in the event of non satisfaction of the decretal dues the court may fall upon the other properly of the other defendant. The property mortgaged in the present case admittedly belongs to defendant No. 3, the guarantor and as such the learned Single Judge of the High Court Division correctly held that the property of the debtor is to be sold first and then the property of the guarantor may be attached and sold if the decree is not satisfied. Defendant No. 2 being the debtor, the learned Single Judge of the High Court Division correctly held that under Rule 5 of Order 34 of the Code of Civil Procedure the court can order for sale of any property of defendant No. 2 first. Defendant No. 2 being the debtor the order that was affirmed by the High Court Division was just proper and fair in the facts and circumstances of the case.
